messages:
sam: Heads-up — ap-south GPU pool provisioning is failing in the new canary batch. Nodes boot but fail during agent start, we see KMS decrypt errors and connections dropped by firewall rules.
maya: seeing same, warm-pool churn is high: new nodes never register.
nikhil: logs? paste the startup trace please.
sam: paste logs below: 
```
2024-06-12T07:12:03Z agent: attempt to load secrets failed: KMS.DecryptAccessDenied: Access denied for key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:111:key/xxxx
2024-06-12T07:12:03Z network: tcp connect to kms.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com:443 -> connection reset by peer
2024-06-12T07:12:04Z bootstrap: aborting node bootstrap, marking UNHEALTHY
```
elle: sec-bot reported a firewall hardening change ~07:00 that applied an egress SNI inspection rule and tied down the NAT egress to a smaller CIDR.
elaine: @sec-bot any idea which rule?
sec-bot: I pushed change FWL-2024-AP-NAT-TIGHTEN at 06:58 to reduce NAT egress range for compliance. It accidentally removed the kms endpoint allow-range for ap-south.
maya: that explains the TCP resets. The KMS key policy also got a tweak last week that added condition on source VPC. If the NAT IP changed nodes can't decrypt.
nikhil: So two simultaneous changes: egress CIDR tightened + key policy referencing old VPC egress IPs. Double fail.
sam: Correct. Also noticed audit logs for that window are sparse — seems logship to central S3 missed a few files (likely due to the same egress pruning).
elaine: Cost impact: warm-pool keep trying to spin gpu nodes and then fail — we're incurring instance ACL + snapshot costs, and customer-facing scaling is impacted. Rough estimate: ~150 hours of wasted GPU time so far.
maya: mitigation options: 1) revert FWL rule (fast) 2) add temporary egress allow for kms endpoints + privatelink IPs (fast) 3) roll back KMS key policy to include new NATs (requires IAM review).
sam: can we short-circuit by patching warm-pool bootstrap to use fallback key in us-west temporarily? Risky.
nikhil: Not ideal; cross-region decryption increases latency and might break auditing. Avoid unless we exhaust other options.
elaine: Action: @nikhil and @maya — add ephemeral egress allow to kms endpoints + re-open NAT CIDR to previous range for 10m. I'll coordinate with sec for an immediate rollback if we confirm fix.
nikhil: on it. Pushing temporary ACL right now.
maya: I'm updating warm-pool bootstrap to include retry/backoff and a clearer error state to stop repeated churn. Patch will be 1.2.4-canary.
sec-bot: Note: rolling back FWL-2024-AP-NAT-TIGHTEN requires approval from security leads; however, we can add an emergency exception rule while we triage.
sam: @elaine can you request emergency exception? tagging legal and compliance per runbook.
elaine: request created: EXC-8342, pinged compliance. Also opened an incident for missing audit logs: INC-2024-AP-LOGDROP.
sam: timeline: temporary egress allow in 3m, warm-pool patch in 10m, key policy rollback after approval (target 2h).
maya: quick note — any chance the keystore HSM is rate limiting? logs show 429s before the TCP resets.
nikhil: 429 likely from retries after connect refused. We'll monitor the KMS metric: kms:Throttles.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: ACL change applied to ap-south NAT gateway in 00:02:37. Rolling exception rule id: EXC-8342-EP.
sam: after exception was added, new nodes started finishing bootstrap and registered. We'll keep canary for 30m to ensure stability.
elaine: follow-ups: (1) add unit test for warm-pool to detect KMS path connectivity before committing. (2) audit current key policies for reliance on fixed egress IPs. (3) update runbook to include cross-check before egress CIDR tightening.
maya: documenting steps in the incident ticket.
sam: thanks all. If compliance ok with exception, close incident after 2h stable. :thumbsup:
